messages.content: My sister confirmed they can pick us up at O’Hare, but only if we land before about 10 p.m. Can we settle the Chicago tickets now? The late nonstop plus airport hotel is starting to feel silly if there’s a cleaner option.

Yes. With that pickup cutoff, I’d compare three paths: the earlier DEN-ORD nonstop around 6:35 p.m. that lands just before 10, the cheaper one-stop with a tight holiday connection, or the later nonstop plus an airport hotel. The earlier nonstop is the cleanest; the one-stop is the fare saver but carries the most risk on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
How much more are we talking for the earlier nonstop? There are two of us, so I’m not ignoring it, but I really don’t want a missed connection mess.

For two adults, the earlier nonstop is roughly $300-$330 more total than the tight one-stop. The late nonstop plus a cancellable ORD-area hotel only saves a small amount once the hotel is included, and it gives you a midnight arrival/check-in. So the real question is whether $300-ish is worth avoiding a sub-hour connection during holiday traffic.
Is the cheap one-stop under an hour? That’s the part making me nervous.

Yes, it’s in the 50-minute range. On an ordinary Tuesday I’d call it workable but not relaxing. On Thanksgiving Wednesday, with a family pickup cutoff and limited later seats if the first leg slips, I would not pick it unless the savings were much bigger.
Okay, that answers it. Let’s pay for the earlier nonstop into O’Hare.

Good call. For the return, you still have the ORD versus Midway choice. Midway is a little cheaper, but from Arlington Heights it adds a much longer drive for your family. The ORD Sunday evening nonstop costs a bit more but keeps both airports consistent and should be much easier for drop-off.
How much are we saving with Midway?

About $100-$130 total for both of you. That’s not nothing, but it likely means an extra 40-plus minutes of driving each way for your relatives on a Sunday evening. I’d keep the return at O’Hare unless you’re trying to squeeze every dollar out of this.
No, keep O’Hare. Economy but not basic. And if there’s a window with the two of us together, great, but don’t split us up for it.

Bookable plan: Wednesday Nov 25, DEN to ORD, nonstop around 6:35 p.m., arriving just before 10 p.m. Sunday Nov 29, ORD to DEN, nonstop around 6:05 p.m., arriving Denver around 8 p.m. Two adults in regular economy/main cabin. Seat choice: adjacent pair first, window/aisle pair if available. Drop the airport-hotel backup once the tickets are issued.
Great. I’m ticketing that now. What should I text my sister?

Send her: We booked the earlier O’Hare nonstop for Wednesday and should land just before 10 p.m. I’ll send the flight number after ticketing. We’re also returning from O’Hare Sunday evening, so no Midway logistics. We’ll text when we land and again once we’re headed to baggage claim or the pickup area. After you buy, cancel the ORD hotel hold and save the airline confirmation.

messages.content: Back to work trips. I need a first pass for the Portland rollout, Jan 19-22. Fly in Monday, train Tuesday through Thursday. The client still hasn’t confirmed whether the room is in Beaverton or Clackamas, and there may be a Monday afternoon equipment check.
Got it. Before I rank anything: what nightly cap should I stay near, and will you have a rental car? Also, if the equipment check happens Monday, what time would you need to be onsite?
Cap is about $225 before tax. I’ll have a rental car. If the check happens, they were talking about 3:30, so I don’t want to land at 3 and sprint.

Then I’d anchor the flight search around a nonstop that lands at PDX around 1 p.m. That gives you time to get the rental car and still make a 3:30 check. I can include cheaper later flights, but they only make sense if the client confirms there is no Monday check.

That sounds right. For hotels, shortest commute wins once we know the site. But I don’t want a sketchy low-rated place. Around 4 stars or better, and I need a gym. Pool or hot tub is a bonus if it stays near cap.

Here’s the first-pass structure. Flight base for either site: Monday DEN-PDX nonstop around 11:15 a.m.-1:05 p.m.; Thursday PDX-DEN nonstop after 5:30 p.m. so you have room after the last class. I’d skip the one-stop options for now; the savings look modest and they add connection risk before a possible setup day.
Okay. What hotels would you put with each possible site?

If Beaverton is confirmed: first look at Embassy Suites by Hilton Portland Washington Square/Tigard, roughly $199-$224 pre-tax when available, about 4.1 on Google, with fitness, indoor pool, and hot tub. Commute to many Beaverton sites is usually 10-20 minutes. Backup: AC Hotel Portland Beaverton, often strong reviews around 4.5 and a good west-side location, but it is more gym-only and can run just over cap.
And Clackamas?

If Clackamas is confirmed: Courtyard Portland Southeast/Clackamas is the practical pick, usually around $185-$215 pre-tax, about 4.1-4.2 on Google, close to the Town Center/Sunnyside area, with fitness and a pool; hot tub is unclear or may be missing. Backup: Residence Inn Portland Clackamas if the rate is close, better room setup and breakfast, but not as strong on recovery amenities.
What about splitting the difference downtown until they tell me? Or is that just worst of both worlds?

Downtown is a hedge, not a great one. It can put you 25-45 minutes from either site depending on traffic, and parking may push the total above cap. I’d only use a downtown cancellable hotel if the client drags this out and both suburban options sell out. For a training week, being on the correct side of Portland matters more.
Can I hold two cancellable hotels without making a mess?

Yes, if your booking system allows it and you track the deadlines. Cleaner plan: ask the client today for the exact address. If they can’t confirm by tomorrow, hold one fully cancellable Beaverton/Tigard room and one fully cancellable Clackamas room, both pay-at-hotel if possible. Cancel the wrong-side reservation as soon as the site is confirmed.
Which two would you hold if it comes to that?

Hold these two if rates cooperate: Embassy Suites Portland Washington Square/Tigard for the Beaverton scenario because it fits the cap and has gym, pool, and hot tub; Courtyard Portland Southeast/Clackamas for the Clackamas scenario because the commute is easiest and the reviews are solid, even if the hot tub is likely the amenity gap.
Should I book the flight now or wait until the site is nailed down too?

The flight is safe to book if Portland is definite: Monday nonstop landing around 1 p.m., Thursday nonstop after 5:30 p.m. The hotel should wait for the address unless you use cancellable holds. Ask the client for four things before booking lodging: exact training address, whether the Monday 3:30 equipment check is definite, parking/loading instructions, and Thursday end time. If they don’t answer by Friday, hold the two cancellable hotels and keep the earlier-arrival flight.
